Hi Sam / Katy,

Thanks again for taking the time today


really enjoyed the conversation and getting a clearer picture of the 3 user flows you flagged (customer support triage, summary + routing, and short-form knowledge search). Per our demo and the evaluation criteria you shared, I put together a short recommended model shortlist and next steps so your team can move into an eval. High-level rationale is included (cost / latency / quality tradeoffs).

Top recommended models for initial eval (ranked):
1) LlamaX-7B-Quant (recommended)

best balance of cost and latency for inference at your target 2

4s p95; strong on extractive QA and short summaries when paired with our prompt tuning.
2) OpenChat-13B-8bit

higher quality on nuance/longer-turn conversation; expect ~2x cost vs 7B but better few-shot performance on your complex escalation examples.
3) GPT-Style-3B-Fast

low-cost option for scaling high-throughput scoring/reranking; lower generation quality but excellent latency and cost for bulk classification tasks.

Attachments / links I included:
- redwood_benchmarks_acme_20260529.pdf

benchmarks (latency p50/p95, tokens/sec) with your sample workload
- acme_prompt_set_v1.csv

canonical prompts + eval slices we recommend using for regression checks
- acme_cost_modeling_20260529.xlsx

estimated per-token cost & monthly projection at your expected volume
- HubSpot deal link and Drive folder with raw eval outputs

Suggested next steps:
- Your team: pick 1

2 models to run the evaluation harness on (we recommend LlamaX-7B-Quant + OpenChat-13B if you want to prioritize quality)
- Redwood: we


ll provision a 7-day eval pool and seed the prompt set + sample traffic if you want (we can also run a canary with your staging data)
- Milestone: 1 week of evals > quick quality check and cost/latency data; follow-up call to decide commit/next steps

A couple of notes on tradeoffs and risks:
- Quality regressions: we recommend keeping your regression test set (the prompt_set_v1) and gating releases 

we

ll wire alerts into the console so you get immediate regression notifications when model outputs deviate from baseline metrics.
- Latency/cost knobs: batching and KV prefix caching give good unit cost reductions for your long-conversation flows; if p95 latency slips we can adjust routing policy to prefer dedicated capacity for the most latency-sensitive routes.

Would you like us to spin up the eval pool and drop the prompt set into your Drive folder? If so, I

ll loop in Aditya and Monica to coordinate access and timing.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0199

Hi Sam

quick answers inline and attaching the benchmark + cost workbook for more detail.

1) Latency numbers: the attached PDF contains our Redwood-hosted lab runs using your sample prompt distribution (we re-played the snippets you shared). The p95 numbers for LlamaX-7B-Quant are ~2.4s under a 12 token/sec average tokenization profile; OpenChat-13B is ~3.8s p95 on the same hardware. Notes: we ran with conservative batching; if you need lower p95 we can shift to lower batch windows or dedicated capacity which reduces p95 at the expense of throughput optimization.

2) Cost delta: see acme_cost_modeling_20260529.xlsx 


ballpark: LlamaX-7B-Quant ~$120 / 1M tokens (hosted) vs OpenChat-13B-8bit ~ $240 / 1M tokens. These are hosted estimates including Redwood margin; Dedicated pricing can be arranged if you want a lower unit cost at commit. Hallucination risk: on your sample prompts we saw comparable hallucination rates for factual QA; OpenChat-13B produced slightly more coherent long-form responses but also longer tails where it hallucinates with higher confidence. We marked those examples in the Drive folder.

3) Eval pool access: we can accept sanitized transcripts and a small sample of staging traffic (TLS; no PII). For provisioning we just need a staging API key and a small S3 bucket of transcripts (or share via Drive). Monica will handle the onboarding and will set up the eval harness + guardrails.

Next: Monica 

can you provision a 7-day eval pool for Acme and drop the initial prompt_set_v1 into the Drive folder mentioned above? Aditya 

can you coordinate the canary plan if they want a routing policy change during evals?

Thanks 


I attached the two files and copied the Drive link in the related links.

Best,
Marissa
